## Amplitude {#fgt1-amplitude .trig-lesson}

The **amplitude** is the maximum vertical distance from the midline.

```{=html}
<div data-trig="amplitude" class="trig-demo"></div>
```

<p class="booklet-cue">Section 1.3 · A sine or cosine graph has amplitude <span data-math="|\textcolor{#b55224}{a}|">|a|</span>.</p>

::: notes

New terminology. This is a static illustration: the graph, dashed midline and double-headed amplitude arrow are visible immediately, with no questions or reveal controls. The illustration $y=2\sin x+1$ is additional, not a numbered booklet example. Explain that the midline is $y=1$ and the vertical distance from that line to a peak at $y=3$ is $2$, the amplitude. The full peak-to-trough distance is $4$, twice the amplitude; amplitude is not the maximum $y$-value. A negative $a$ reflects the graph before translation; for example, $y=-2\sin x+1$ still has amplitude $2$. Tangent is unbounded and has no amplitude; return to this on the tangent slide. Keep this explanation brief.

:::
